label: Alderney

about.text: A dairy breed from Alderney in the Channel Islands, named for the island. It was kept for rich milk and butter-making, and was used for draught work before horses replaced oxen. The breed was absorbed into the Guernsey breed after the Second World War and is now listed as extinct.

sources.text: Summarised from the Wikipedia page (revision of 11 June 2026): the island origin, the draught and butter history, the absorption into Guernsey, and the extinct listing. The word 'small' is not stated on that page and is left out of the text.

The Wikipedia page places the breed on Alderney in the Channel Islands. The Channel Islands are not in countries.json, so GB (the nearest listed code, the United Kingdom) is used as a stand-in; the Channel Islands are not part of the UK, so this code is approximate.
The Wikipedia page lists the breed as extinct and gives no FAO DAD-IS entry or year. The Wikipedia page says it was absorbed into Guernsey after the Second World War.

facts.v: 580 animals were registered in 1910, kept by 75 farmers, about half of whom had four or fewer cattle.

sources.text: As stated on the Wikipedia page. This is a registration count from 1910, not a current population.

facts.v: Cattle may have been introduced to the Channel Islands by monks from Mont-Saint-Michel, reportedly sent around AD 960 by Richard I of Normandy.

sources.text: The Wikipedia page gives this as a possibility and says 'reportedly', so the claim is kept hedged.

facts.v: The breed contributed to the Ayrshire and South Devon, and possibly to the Dairy Shorthorn, Kerry and Suffolk Dun.

sources.text: As stated on the Wikipedia page.
